story: Grocery Outlet is grinding up a rising channel that runs from about $11.49 to $13.95, and it has won back 69% of its collapse from $16.37 to $5.66. Today's 1.8% gain to $13.02 cleared the last swing high on a trend of higher highs and higher lows. The averages are stacked and rising: the 10-day at $12.46, the 20-day at $11.88, which held its retest on Oct 7, the 50-day at $11.65 and the 200-day at $9.42. A support line near $11.60 sits right with the 50-day, and the top of the high-volume range at $12.38 is now support too.

This is a leader: the six-month gain of 65% beats 96% of stocks, it is 36.1 points ahead of the S&P 500 over three months, and consumer staples lead the sector map. ADX at 30 confirms the trend, RSI rose to 68 from 66, and MACD is above zero and its signal line. Insider buying, heavy short interest and a strong earnings reaction all line up, with holders since the Aug 12 earnings report averaging $11.61. Volume is light at 0.71× normal, price moving easily with nothing in the way, but it is stretched 3.0 daily ranges above the 50-day, more than 89% of its past year. The channel top and weekly swing high at $13.95 is the bigger ceiling. A strong trend best bought at the 20-day.

story: IQVIA is a few percent from its 52-week high of $277.40, closing at $267.85 on a trend that has added 52% in six months and beats 95% of stocks. The structure is a clean staircase of higher highs and higher lows. Today price dipped into the support zone from $262.30 to $266.80, retested the 20-day at $265.00 and held, leaving an outside bar with a wick rejection that closed back up. The 50-day at $261.10 held its own retest on Oct 13, a support line runs near $264.40, and the busiest price of the past month at $261.70 sits right on the 50-day. That is three or four floors packed into a few dollars.

Volume ran 1.34× normal on the dip-and-recover day, and the Bollinger bands had been squeezed into the narrowest fifth of the year before today's release. RSI rose to 56 from 54 with a hidden bullish divergence building, while MACD has flattened onto its signal line above zero, a pause rather than a turn. Over three months the stock is 32.0 points ahead of the S&P 500 and health care leads the sector map, though the last month has only matched SPY. Holders since the Jul 28 earnings report average $257.03, and profit rose to $274.0M on 8.4% revenue growth. The weekly swing high at $272.25 is the hurdle before the old high. The room to the target is only modest, so the fill has to come at the busiest price, not above it.
